more.def: A reddish-brown color, often used for hair.
examples: Her auburn hair shone in the sun.
The auburn leaves fell in October.
An auburn horse stood in the field.

easy.def: A sale where people bid to buy things.

more.def: A public sale in which people offer prices and the highest offer wins.
examples: We went to an auction to buy an old clock.
The auction was held in the barn.
The painting sold at auction for a high price.

easy.def: A person who sells things at an auction by calling out prices.

more.def: A person who sells things to the highest bidder by calling out prices.
examples: The auctioneer talked fast as the prices rose.
An auctioneer sold the old chair.

more.def: Bold and daring, often in a way that surprises people.
examples: It was an audacious plan to cross the river.
The audacious boy asked for a second cake.
The audacious leap amazed the crowd.
He had the audacity to ask.

more.def: A bold willingness to take risks, or rude boldness.
examples: He had the audacity to ask for a second cake.
It took audacity to speak up.
The audacity of the fox amazed the farmer.

more.def: Loud enough to be heard.
examples: The soft music was barely audible over the sound of the rain.
Her whisper was audible all the way to the back of the room.
An audible hum came from the old refrigerator.

easy.def: In a way that can be heard.

more.def: In a way that can be heard.
examples: She sighed audibly when the bell rang.
He gulped audibly before he spoke.

easy.def: The people who watch or listen to a show.
examples: The audience sat in the dark.
A big audience came to the play.

more.def: A group of people who gather to watch or listen to a show or talk.
examples: The audience laughed at the funny clown.
The band played to a huge audience in the park.
The audience stood up and cheered at the end of the concert.
I listen to an audio book.

more.def: Having to do with sound that is recorded or played back.
examples: I listened to an audio book in the car.
The audio on the video was clear.

more.def: Using both sound and pictures.
examples: The teacher used an audiovisual aid in class.
The audiovisual show had music and film.
The school has an audiovisual room with a big screen.

easy.def: A short try-out for a part in a show.
examples: I have an audition for the play.

more.def: A short performance to show a director that you can sing, act or play.
examples: I have an audition for the school play.
She sang a song at her audition.
The band held auditions for a new drummer.

easy.def: A big room where people sit to watch a show.

more.def: A large hall with rows of seats where people gather to watch a show, hear a talk or attend a meeting.
examples: The whole school met in the auditorium for the play.
The auditorium has a stage and rows of seats.
The band played in the school auditorium.
We go to the lake in August.

more.def: The eighth month of the year, near the end of summer.
examples: Many families take trips to the beach in August.
The sunflowers are tall by August.
In some places, school starts again in late August.

easy.def: The sister of your mom or dad.

more.def: The sister of your mother or father, or the wife of your uncle.
examples: My aunt taught me to knit.
Both of my aunts came to the party.

more.def: A friendly word for aunt.
examples: My auntie came to visit us.
I called my auntie on her birthday.

easy.def: A special feeling that seems to come from a person or place.
examples: The old house had a strange aura.
The room had a happy aura.

more.def: A feeling or mood that seems to surround a person or place.
examples: The quiet old library had an aura of peace.
The champion walked in with an aura of confidence.
The dark woods had a strange aura that made us whisper.

easy.def: Bright colored lights in the night sky.

more.def: Bands of colored light that glow in the night sky near the North or South Pole.
examples: We watched green and purple lights of the aurora dance across the sky.
The aurora can be seen in places where it is very cold.
Auroras happen when tiny bits from the sun hit the air high above Earth.

more.def: Giving signs that things will turn out well.
examples: It was an auspicious start to the season.
The bright morning was an auspicious sign.

more.def: Very plain and simple, without comforts or decoration.
examples: The austere room had only a bed and a chair.

easy.def: A country and continent in the southern part of the world.

more.def: A country and continent south of Asia, between the Indian and Pacific oceans.
examples: Kangaroos and koalas live in Australia.
We found Australia on the map.
This is an authentic Native American drum.
We ate authentic pizza in Italy.

more.def: Real and true, not made up or copied.
examples: The museum has an authentic suit of armor from long ago.
We ate authentic pizza in a little restaurant in Italy.
An expert checked that the painting was authentic.

more.def: A person who writes books, stories or articles.
examples: The author signed copies of her book.
My favorite author writes about dragons.

easy.def: Trusted because it comes from an expert.

more.def: Trusted and respected because it comes from someone who knows a lot.
examples: The dictionary is an authoritative book.
She spoke in an authoritative voice.
He is an authoritative source on birds.

easy.def: The power to tell people what to do.

more.def: The power or right to give orders and make decisions.
examples: The captain has authority over the ship.
The police have authority to stop cars.
A parent has authority over the family.

more.def: To give official permission for something.
examples: The principal authorized the field trip.
The mayor authorized the building of the park.
Only the guard can authorize you to enter.

more.def: The fact of being the writer of a book or other work.
examples: The authorship of the old poem is unknown.
He claimed authorship of the story.
Authorship tells who wrote a book.

more.def: A short, old-fashioned word for a car.
examples: We rode in an auto to the lake.
The auto sped down the road.

more.def: Telling the story of the writer's own life.
examples: She wrote an autobiographical story about her childhood.
Her first novel is partly autobiographical.
His autobiographical essay described his school days.

easy.def: A book a person writes about their own life.

more.def: The story of a person's life, written by that person.
examples: She wrote an autobiography about growing up on a farm.
I read the autobiography of a famous scientist.
In an autobiography, the writer tells his own story.

easy.def: A tool that fixes your spelling by itself.

more.def: A feature on phones and computers that fixes spelling mistakes for you as you type.
examples: The autocorrect changed my word to a different one.
Autocorrect is helpful but not always right.

easy.def: A famous person's name written by themselves.
examples: The autograph is on the poster.

more.def: A person's own signature, especially a famous person's, that they write for a fan.
examples: I asked the player for his autograph.
The singer signed an autograph for a fan.
My brother has the autograph of a pilot.

more.def: Signed by a famous person with their own name.
examples: He kept the autographed baseball on a shelf.
The author handed me an autographed copy of her book.
An autographed picture of the singer hung on the wall.

easy.def: A stringed instrument you strum with buttons for chords.

more.def: A stringed instrument with buttons that let you strum chords.
examples: An autoharp has buttons that mute some strings.
The teacher played songs on the autoharp.

easy.def: To make a machine do the job.

more.def: To use machines or computers to do a job instead of people.
examples: The factory automated the packing of boxes.
The farm automated the watering of its crops.

more.def: Working on its own without a person controlling it.
examples: The automatic door opened as we walked up.
The light is automatic and turns on at night.
The machine has an automatic shut-off.

more.def: In a way that happens by itself without anyone controlling it.
examples: The door opens automatically as you walk up.
The lights turn on automatically at dusk.

more.def: The use of machines to do work that people used to do.
examples: The factory uses automation to build cars.

more.def: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries people.
examples: The automobile sped down the road.
We rode in an old automobile.
He works in an automotive shop.

more.def: Having to do with cars and other motor vehicles.
examples: He works in an automotive repair shop.
The school has an automotive class.
The museum has an automotive display.

easy.def: Able to work or act alone.

more.def: Able to act or run on its own without being controlled by someone else.
examples: An autonomous robot cleans the floor.
The region is autonomous and makes its own laws.

easy.def: A system that flies a plane by itself.

more.def: A device that steers a plane or ship without a person doing the work.
examples: The pilot turned on the autopilot during the long flight.
The ship was on autopilot while the crew rested.
I did my chores on autopilot without thinking.

easy.def: The season between summer and winter, when leaves fall.

more.def: The season between summer and winter, when the weather turns cooler and leaves fall from the trees; also called fall.
examples: Leaves turn red and gold in autumn.
We pick apples and pumpkins in autumn.

more.def: Having to do with autumn, or like autumn.
examples: It was a cool, autumnal day.

more.def: Giving extra help or support; spare.
examples: The ship had an auxiliary engine.
An auxiliary light came on when the power failed.
The auxiliary team helped when the main team was tired.
